cards.why: F-1: the Office of Levee Inspection decided on 24 July 2026, by a letter that came only by mail and was scanned on 6 October (M-1): 3 of 12 reports released, 9 withheld in full. Filerecords still shows the request open. The appeal lies within 90 days of the letter's date, so its last day is Thursday 22 October 2026 (24 July plus 90 days); BD-2 says to appeal a determination on a request the project still needs. Count weight 1

F-3: the Lead Pipe Replacement Program Office put the project in the commercial-use category, 'because the request names a private contractor' (letter of 15 September 2026). A commercial use furthers the requester's own commercial, trade or profit interest; the project is a nonprofit that publishes reports and a free newsletter, takes no advertising and has no interest in the contractor (BD-1), which makes it a representative of the news media who pays duplication only. A fee decision is appealable within 90 days of the letter, to Monday 14 December 2026. Count weight 1

F-4: the Regional Housing Quality Service denied the fee waiver (letter of 2 September 2026). The project will publish the scores of 40 housing complexes free, in a table and a report (BD-3), which is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the government's operations and is not in its commercial interest. A fee decision is appealable within 90 days of the letter, to Tuesday 1 December 2026. Count weight 1

F-6: received Tuesday 1 September 2026, so its 20 working days ended on Wednesday 30 September (Labor Day, Monday 7 September, does not count); no extension was noticed and nothing has come since the acknowledgment. It is 7 working days overdue. A message to the agency's FOIA Public Liaison asking for its status and estimated completion date is what 552(a)(7)(B) and (a)(6)(B)(ii) give. Count weight 1

F-8: the Regional Housing Quality Service's notice of 31 August 2026 offers to limit the request to the project office's 2 custodians for 2024 to 2026, as 552(a)(6)(B)(ii) requires it to offer, and will treat the request as withdrawn if it hears nothing by Friday 23 October 2026. BD-2 allows narrowing on an agency's offer in its terms. Count weight 1

DR-1: approved by the director on 2 October 2026 and not filed; no open request asks for the 2026 lead line inventory submissions of 5 utilities (F-7 asks for correspondence with 2 utilities about their inventories). Count weight 1

C-3: the city asks 584 dollars, of which 572 is staff time to search and review. Gov. Code 7922.530(a) allows only the direct costs of duplication, and searching and reviewing are not that; the 120 copies at 10 cents are 12 dollars. A message asking for release on payment of 12 dollars is right. Count weight 1

C-4: received Monday 14 September 2026, so the 10 days of Gov. Code 7922.535(a) ended on Thursday 24 September; no extension notice was sent and no answer has come. A message asking for the determination and the estimated date is the Act's remedy short of court. Count weight 1
